Round 354 is closed as a pass, and the round-355 task is written and ready for A. The decision is **CONTINUE**: nothing outside the loop is blocking it.

**Round 354 (evidence only)**
- C passed it with browser checks done and 0 bugs. All 82 asserted perf rows passed, with no new rows and nothing above round 350's values.
- Root published it as `7219291` on both remotes. That commit is the starting point for round 355.
- I saved the old task as `tasks/round-354.md` (a copy; nothing deleted). Backlog is now v318 (D-29z1140…D-29z1144), and `feature-status.md` marks the video trim/fade stage 2 as მზადაა.
- One fake-token check returned 500 instead of 403 because the mock backend isn't running in the cloud. It failed closed and stays open as backend evidence, not a bug.
- C's own extra mutant changed nothing, so it isn't evidence that the new rows catch regressions. I recorded that as info only.
- Gate reviewer findings:
  - The leftover "Record until…" wording in the 12 budget notes moves into the next budgets-only task.
  - The near-zero headroom on two budgets is intended and closed.
  - The suggestion to split doc 232 is recorded as an architecture note for the pending checkpoint, not scheduled.

**Round 355 = SYS-R353-DP-TEST-POLISH (test file + doc 232 only, no app code)**
It closes four Low findings from earlier code reviews:
- **DP69:** the release must now write nothing to the video fade overlay. This replaces a check that repeated another one.
- **DP70:** the caption check compared an empty string with an empty string, so it could never fail; it is removed, and DP64 already covers the caption. The gap checks now use a committed trim that uncovers the playhead, then Undo and Redo.
- **DP72:**
  - the drag must move more than 0.01 s;
  - the committed start must match the preview exactly, checked before the seek count;
  - the fixed 20 ms wait is replaced by fake timers that run every pending `setTimeout`.
- **The `'Video Fade In'` label stays as a literal.** Exporting it would change app code.
- **What DP72 still doesn't cover is written into doc 232:** writes scheduled through `requestAnimationFrame` (stubbed in this file), timer references saved when a module loads, and the playing path.

I tested this on my own scratch copy, never in `store/`:
- The edited file passes 74/74, plus Biome, typecheck, and two shuffled-order runs. In one of them 46 tests ran after DP72.
- Every tightened check has a deliberately broken version of the code that fails on the new test and passes on the current one. Results are in `b-round-354/sketch/mutant-summary.txt`.
- Both patches recreate the edited files byte for byte on a fresh copy of `7219291`.
- tech-lead found nothing Medium or above; I fixed three of its Lows in the sketch.

**Also recorded**
- The 2026-11-05 parallel-execution policy wasn't in the backlog yet, so I added it (D-29z1143). Round 355 doesn't touch root's lanes (export dialog, toolbar, docs). The claims script accepts a HEAD that only adds root-lane commits on top of `7219291`.
- The round-352 dock finding that waits for "the next task that touches the dock" is not triggered, because round 355 doesn't touch it.

**Next after 355:** the video-move budget task (including the note wording fix), then the master/group fader task if the architecture checkpoint has been answered, otherwise the fade release-commits task or PERF-9. Any planning on or after 2026-11-08 runs the regression round first.

The advisor was available. I used it before the substantive work and again at the close; the closing call led to four fixes, all applied.
